title: Crucible of Creation: Panoramic Image of Center of the Orion Nebula
caption: The center of the Orion Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Orion Nebula, M42, NGC 1976 · constellation Orion · about 1,500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, C.R. O'Dell and S.K. Wong (Rice University)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Glowing gas rises into peaks, valleys and walls across this panorama of the center of the Orion Nebula, a star-forming region 1,500 light-years away in the sword of Orion. Stitched from a mosaic of 15 fields, it was at the time one of the largest pictures ever assembled from Hubble images.

The view spans 2.5 light-years yet covers only about five percent of the full Moon's area on the sky. Near the center sit the Trapezium, the nebula's four hottest and most massive stars, whose ultraviolet light heats and lights the gas. Some 700 other young stars are forming here, and jets from some of them drive shock waves that show up as thin curved loops.

The mosaic also revealed at least 153 glowing protoplanetary disks, or proplyds, thought to be embryonic solar systems. Those nearest the Trapezium are losing gas and dust, pushed into tails that point away from the hot stars. Seven more disks appear as dark silhouettes, which let astronomers estimate disk masses of at least 0.1 to 730 times Earth's mass.

understand.summary: A mosaic of 45 visible-light images from Hubble's Wide Field Planetary Camera 2. Light emitted by oxygen is shown in blue, hydrogen in green and nitrogen in red.
understand.eye: NASA says the overall color balance is close to what an observer living near the nebula would see.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, C.R. O'Dell and S.K. Wong (Rice University)
behind.exposure: Observation dates per NASA: January 1994 and March 1995.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The stars here formed from collapsing clouds of gas within the last million years. C. Robert O'Dell of Rice University and Shui Kwan Wong combined 45 separate images to make the mosaic. Images from the European Southern Observatory by Bo Reipurth and John Bally fill out the irregular border at top left.
sources: NASA release: Panoramic Hubble Picture Surveys Star Birth, Proto-Planetary Systems in the Great Orion Nebula
alt: A wide panorama of glowing, folded gas clouds in the heart of the Orion Nebula, with bright young stars near the center.
